boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Biola University
boards.description: From on-campus coffee houses to local diners, these late-night spots provide the essential fuel for Biola students during late study sessions and post-event gatherings.

cards.title: Common Grounds
cards.subtitle: On-Campus Coffee House
cards.notes: Grab a late-night espresso or fruit smoothie at this central campus hub, often open until 1 a.m. for study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A cozy on-campus coffee lounge located on the east patio of the Student Union Building.
cards.evidence_claim: Common Grounds is open Monday to Friday until 1 a.m. and serves as a late-night study fuel spot.
cards.source_title: On Campus Dining Locations - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday until 1:00 AM; Saturday and Sunday until 12:00 AM.

cards.title: Eagles' Nest
cards.subtitle: Campus Diner & Grille
cards.notes: Visit this classic campus diner for burgers and late-night quesadillas, serving the student body until midnight.
cards.short_summary: A classic diner and grille located in the Student Union Building featuring burgers and a taqueria.
cards.evidence_claim: Eagles' Nest offers a late-night menu from 9 p.m. to 12 a.m. daily.
cards.source_title: Eagles' Nest | Offices & Services, Biola University
cards.access_notes: Late night hours are 9:00 PM to 12:00 AM daily.

cards.title: In-N-Out Burger
cards.subtitle: Iconic California Drive-Thru
cards.notes: Drive over to Firestone Blvd for a Double-Double at this local staple, a favorite for post-Singspiration snacks.
cards.short_summary: A classic Southern California burger chain located approximately 2.5 miles from campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The La Mirada In-N-Out location on Firestone Blvd is open until 1:00 AM daily (1:30 AM on Fri/Sat).
cards.source_title: La Mirada, CA, 14341 Firestone Blvd. - In-N-Out Burger
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 1:30 AM Friday-Saturday.

cards.title: Raising Cane's
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Chicken Fingers
cards.notes: Head to nearby La Habra for a Box Combo; the drive-thru stays busy with students well past midnight.
cards.short_summary: A popular fast-food chain specializing in chicken fingers, located just south of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The La Habra location on Beach Blvd is open until 3:00 AM or 3:30 AM most nights.
cards.source_title: Raising Cane's in La Habra, CA - 1050 S Beach Blvd
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:00 AM Sunday-Wednesday and 3:30 AM Thursday-Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell
cards.subtitle: Budget-Friendly Late Bites
cards.notes: A go-to for affordable late-night tacos and burritos, located conveniently on La Mirada Blvd.
cards.short_summary: A fast-food restaurant offering Mexican-inspired fare with late-night drive-thru service.
cards.evidence_claim: The Taco Bell at 15006 La Mirada Blvd is open until 2:00 AM or 3:00 AM.
cards.source_title: Taco Bell in La Mirada, CA - 15006 La Mirada Blvd.
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru open until 2:00 AM Sunday-Thursday and 3:00 AM Friday-Saturday.

cards.title: Denny's
cards.subtitle: 24-Hour American Diner
cards.notes: The ultimate 24/7 destination for breakfast slams and late-night study breaks off-campus.
cards.short_summary: A full-service 24-hour diner located on Beach Blvd in neighboring La Habra.
cards.evidence_claim: The Denny's on S Beach Blvd is a 24-hour restaurant serving breakfast and dinner all night.
cards.source_title: 24-Hour Diner and Breakfast Restaurant | Denny's
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

cards.title: Starbucks
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Coffee & Study
cards.notes: This nearby Imperial Highway location offers a drive-thru and indoor seating for late-night caffeine runs.
cards.short_summary: A popular coffeehouse chain located at the intersection of La Mirada and Imperial Highway.
cards.evidence_claim: The Starbucks at 15010 Imperial Hwy is known to stay open until 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: Starbucks Coffee Company - La Mirada & Imperial Hwy
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Krispy Kreme
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Doughnut Run
cards.notes: Watch for the 'Hot Now' light at this La Habra location, a sweet destination for late-night group outings.
cards.short_summary: A famous doughnut shop known for its glazed rings, located on Imperial Highway.
cards.evidence_claim: The La Habra Krispy Kreme is open until 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM daily.
cards.source_title: Fresh Doughnuts and Coffee | Krispy Kreme La Habra
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM Sunday-Thursday and 11:00 PM Friday-Saturday.

cards.title: IHOP
cards.subtitle: Late-Night Pancake House
cards.notes: A reliable spot for a late-night stack of pancakes, located just a short drive from the Biola campus.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing chain serving a wide variety of pancakes and other American breakfast and diner fare.
cards.evidence_claim: The IHOP on La Mirada Blvd serves the community with late-night hours, typically until 10:00 PM or later.
cards.source_title: IHOP Breakfast Restaurants Near You at 15140 La Mirada Blvd
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 10:00 PM or later; check local schedule for 24-hour availability.

cards.title: The Habit Burger Grill
cards.subtitle: Chargrilled Late Dinner

cards.evidence_claim: The Habit Burger Grill in La Mirada is a frequent student choice for evening meals.
cards.source_title: La Mirada - Habit Burger & Grill
cards.access_notes: Open daily until 10:00 PM or 11:00 PM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the quiet corners, study retreats, and reflective spaces that define the daily student experience at Biola University beyond the main landmarks.

cards.title: A 24/7 Sanctuary for Quiet Reflection
cards.subtitle: The oldest chapel on campus
cards.notes: Visit this small, historic chapel for uninterrupted silence. It is open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, specifically for individual prayer and reflection.
cards.short_summary: A historic, 24-hour prayer chapel dedicated to silent reflection and individual worship.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rose of Sharon Prayer Chapel is open to students and visitors any time of the day or night, 365 days a year, for quiet time to reflect and pray.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 for individual use; no events are scheduled here to ensure a quiet environment.

cards.entity_name: Fred and Ruth Waugh Prayer Chapel
cards.title: The 'Hidden' Modern Prayer Space
cards.subtitle: Located in the lower level of Talbot East
cards.notes: Look for the discreet door off Haqq Plaza to find this award-winning space featuring a reclaimed wood ceiling and unique 'Bedouin tent' carpeting.
cards.short_summary: An award-winning, modern prayer chapel tucked away in the lower level of the Talbot East building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fred and Ruth Waugh Prayer Chapel is located in the lower level of Talbot East and is open from 7:30 a.m. to midnight daily.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open daily from 7:30 a.m. to midnight.

cards.title: The Historic Olive Grove Retreat
cards.subtitle: Tucked away on the eastern edge of campus
cards.notes: Walk the rustic paths through the remains of a historic olive orchard. It's a quiet spot for a picnic or a break between classes on the campus perimeter.
cards.short_summary: A peaceful park and historic olive grove on the eastern edge of campus featuring walking paths and benches.
cards.evidence_claim: Kavalich Park, also known as the Olive Grove, features rustic walk paths, a walking bridge, benches, and picnic tables on the eastern edge of campus.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor park on the university grounds.

cards.title: The Iconic 'Jesus Mural'
cards.subtitle: On the exterior of the Science Building
cards.notes: View this massive mural created by Kent Twitchell. It is made of thousands of newspaper clippings and is a landmark for students walking toward the Lim Center.
cards.short_summary: A large-scale exterior mural of Jesus Christ, titled 'The Word,' created by artist Kent Twitchell.
cards.evidence_claim: The mural 'The Word,' commonly known as the Jesus Mural, is located on the exterior of the Biola University Science Building.
cards.source_title: Restoration of the Jesus Mural - CCCA
cards.access_notes: Visible from the exterior of the building near the campus center.

cards.title: Focused Study in the Lower Level
cards.subtitle: Quiet zones for group or individual work
cards.notes: Reserve a room online for up to two hours. The lower level rooms are often preferred by students seeking a more secluded environment for intense study sessions.
cards.short_summary: Reservable study rooms located on the upper and lower levels of the main university library.
cards.evidence_claim: Study rooms are located on the upper and lower levels of the library and can be reserved by students for up to two hours per day.
cards.source_title: Library Spaces - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Available during library open hours; reservations are recommended but not required if a room is empty.

cards.title: Shaded Courtyard at Sutherland Hall
cards.subtitle: A quiet outdoor lobby space
cards.notes: Use this shaded outdoor area for a quick meeting or a quiet place to read. It sits just outside the Ethel Lee Auditorium in one of the campus's original buildings.
cards.short_summary: A beautifully shaded outdoor courtyard located adjacent to Sutherland Hall and the Ethel Lee Auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Ethel Lee Auditorium features a beautifully shaded courtyard just outside the auditorium in Sutherland Hall.
cards.source_title: Auditoriums - Venues - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open outdoor courtyard accessible during campus hours.

cards.title: The Haqq Plaza Reflection Pool
cards.subtitle: A serene waterfall and plaza
cards.notes: Pause by the waterfall wall and reflection pool between Talbot East and Calvary Chapel. It's a dedicated space for students to pause and reflect between classes.
cards.short_summary: A plaza featuring a reflection pool and waterfall wall located between Talbot East and Calvary Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The plaza with a reflection pool and waterfall wall provides a serene place for students to pause and reflect, located between Talbot East and Calvary Chapel.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Spiritual Rhythms - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza accessible to the campus community.

cards.title: Alpha Hall's Rooftop Retreat
cards.subtitle: A resident favorite for sun and study
cards.notes: Residents of Alpha Hall can head to the rooftop sundeck for a change of scenery. It's a unique elevated space for hanging out or catching some sun.
cards.short_summary: A rooftop sundeck available for residents of Alpha Hall, offering an outdoor community area.
cards.evidence_claim: Alpha Hall offers a rooftop sundeck as part of its community areas for residents.
cards.source_title: Alpha Hall - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Access is typically restricted to residents of Alpha Hall via electronic key system.

cards.title: The 'StewHart' Shortcut
cards.subtitle: Connecting lower and upper campus
cards.notes: Take these stairs near Stewart and Hart Halls for a quick shortcut to the softball field and the sand volleyball courts. It's a major time-saver for south-campus residents.
cards.short_summary: A set of stairs serving as a shortcut between the residence halls and the upper athletic fields.
cards.evidence_claim: The stairs located next to Stewart's and Hart's bike rack go straight up to the softball field and beach volleyball court.
cards.source_title: Secret Passageways at Biola University - Becoming Biola
cards.access_notes: Outdoor stairs accessible to all pedestrians on campus.

cards.title: The Heart of the Plaza
cards.subtitle: A central gathering and study spot
cards.notes: While iconic, the plaza around the fountain is a primary spot for outdoor studying. Look for the compass on the ground, designed to remind students of the world beyond campus.
cards.short_summary: A central campus plaza featuring the Fluor Fountain, used extensively by students for socializing and outdoor study.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fluor Fountain plaza fulfills the dream of being a place where many students study and hang out.
cards.source_title: Fact of the Week: Fluor Fountain - The Chimes
cards.access_notes: Central outdoor plaza open to the public.

cards.title: Walk the Olive Grove

cards.evidence_claim: Kavalich Park, also known as the Olive Grove, features rustic walk paths and benches for the community.

cards.title: Lounge on the Grass
cards.subtitle: Center of Campus
cards.notes: Gather with friends on the university's largest open green space. It is a popular spot for casual social hangouts, outdoor reading, and campus-wide events.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From a 300-pound concrete egg to a campus-wide dodgeball war, Biola University's traditions reflect its tight-knit community and unique history.

cards.title: Mock Rock
cards.subtitle: The Ultimate Lip-Sync Battle
cards.notes: Join a team of 60 students to choreograph elaborate lip-sync and dance routines. This decades-old competition is live-streamed and offers the ultimate campus bragging rights.
cards.short_summary: Mock Rock is a massive annual lip-syncing and dance competition where student groups perform creative, high-energy stories for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: Mock Rock is an annual lip-syncing contest and one of Biola's favorite traditions, featuring creative stories, dancing, and costumes.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Recreational Activities - Campus Engagement - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the spring; tickets are typically required for the live event in Chase Gymnasium.

cards.title: Nationball
cards.subtitle: Campus-Wide Dodgeball War
cards.notes: Wear your dorm's designated color—like Horton black or Hope pink—and compete in this massive dodgeball tournament to earn spirit points for your residence hall.
cards.short_summary: Nationball is an annual campus-wide dodgeball tournament where residence halls compete for spirit points and the championship title.
cards.evidence_claim: Nationball is a campus-wide dodgeball tournament where dorms face off against each other, with each dorm wearing a specific team color.
cards.source_title: Nine Fun Facts About 'Nationball' - Biola Magazine
cards.access_notes: The event is the first major spirit event of the academic year, typically held in September at Chase Gymnasium.

cards.title: The Biola Egg
cards.subtitle: A 300-Pound Concrete Mystery
cards.notes: Keep an eye out for a massive concrete egg that dorms hide and hunt for. Rules require 50% of the egg to be visible, and its location is often teased on social media.
cards.short_summary: The Biola Egg is a mysterious 300-pound concrete object that has been part of a campus-wide game of hide-and-seek for decades.
cards.evidence_claim: The Biola Egg is a mysterious mass of concrete that students hunt for; it is a long-standing tradition with specific rules for hiding and finding it.
cards.source_title: New rules crack egg tradition - The Chimes
cards.access_notes: The egg is hidden in various public campus locations; students must follow Student Heritage Board (SPA) guidelines for the hunt.

cards.title: Missions Conference
cards.subtitle: World's Largest Student-Led Mission Event
cards.notes: Attend the Parade of Nations and hear from global speakers during this three-day event. Classes are canceled so the entire student body can participate together.
cards.short_summary: The Missions Conference is a massive, student-led annual event that brings global awareness and speakers to campus, resulting in a three-day class cancellation.
cards.evidence_claim: Biola's annual Missions Conference is the largest student-led missions conference in the world, and classes are canceled for the three-day event.
cards.source_title: Cook Missions Conference - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the spring; sessions are open to the Biola community and often streamed online.

cards.title: Punk'N Pie
cards.subtitle: Talent Show and Autumn Treats
cards.notes: Watch your peers perform magic, music, or stunts at this annual talent show. Stay until the end to enjoy a free slice of pumpkin pie with the campus community.
cards.short_summary: Punk'N Pie is Biola's annual fall talent show that concludes with a community-wide pumpkin pie social.
cards.evidence_claim: Punk'N Pie is an annual student talent show featuring various acts, followed by pumpkin pie for attendees.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Recreational Activities - Campus Engagement - Biola University
cards.access_notes: An annual fall tradition; typically held outdoors or in a large campus venue.

cards.title: Christmas Tree Lighting
cards.subtitle: SoCal Snow and Carols
cards.notes: Gather for the lighting of the campus tree, featuring scripture readings, musical performances, and even artificial 'Southern California snow' to start the season.
cards.short_summary: The Christmas Tree Lighting is a beloved annual tradition that brings the campus together for worship, music, and festive treats.
cards.evidence_claim: The annual Christmas Tree Lighting features musical performances, scripture readings, and traditional Southern California snow.
cards.source_title: Christmas Tree Lighting 2024
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December; open to students, alumni, and the public.

cards.title: Torrey Memorial Bible Conference
cards.subtitle: A 90-Year Legacy of Faith
cards.notes: Participate in one of Biola's oldest traditions, featuring themed biblical teaching and the 'Torrey Slam'—a session of personal stories and original music.
cards.short_summary: The Torrey Memorial Bible Conference is a long-standing annual event dedicated to biblical exposition and spiritual formation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Torrey Memorial Bible Conference is one of Biola's longest-lasting traditions, celebrating its 90th annual conference in 2025.
cards.source_title: Biola University's Torrey Memorial Bible Conference is 90 Years Young
cards.access_notes: Held annually in October; sessions take place across campus and are central to student life.

cards.title: The Jesus Mural
cards.subtitle: The Word by Kent Twitchell
cards.notes: Visit this iconic 40-foot mural on the side of the Science Center. It has been a landmark of campus identity and a subject of community conversation since 1990.
cards.short_summary: Known officially as 'The WORD,' this massive mural of Jesus is a central campus landmark created by renowned muralist Kent Twitchell.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jesus Mural, or 'The WORD,' was a project directed by LA muralist Kent Twitchell and finished in 1990; it remains a significant campus landmark.
cards.source_title: Restoration of the Jesus Mural - Biola University Center for Christianity, Culture and the Arts
cards.access_notes: The mural is located on the exterior of the Science Center and is visible to the public.

cards.title: The Eddy
cards.subtitle: Student Concert Series
cards.notes: Take a break from studies at this evening concert series. It features up-and-coming artists and student performers in a relaxed setting with snacks.
cards.short_summary: The Eddy is a recurring concert series that showcases student talent and guest artists in an intimate campus environment.
cards.evidence_claim: The Eddy is a concert series featuring up-and-coming artists and student performers, providing a way for students to enjoy the arts.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Recreational Activities - Campus Engagement - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Occurs periodically throughout the semester; check the campus engagement calendar for dates.

cards.title: Fiesta Latina
cards.subtitle: Hispanic Heritage Celebration
cards.notes: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month with food, music, and dance. This annual event is a collaboration between the Unidos club and the Office of Campus Engagement.
cards.short_summary: Fiesta Latina is an annual community event that celebrates the diverse cultures and stories of the Hispanic community through art and performance.
cards.evidence_claim: Fiesta Latina is an annual community event to celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month, including food, music, dance, and art.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions & Recreational Activities - Campus Engagement - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Held annually during Hispanic Heritage Month (September/October).

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Biola University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Unload at Your New Home
cards.subtitle: Move-In Day Logistics
cards.notes: Arrive during your assigned window to have student leaders and athletes help unload your car and deliver belongings directly to your room.
cards.short_summary: Experience the concierge-style move-in service where volunteers assist new students with their luggage.
cards.evidence_claim: Biola student leaders and over 400 athletes unload new students' cars and deliver belongings straight to their dorm rooms on move-in day.
cards.source_title: Biola University to Welcome First-Year Students Concierge Style
cards.access_notes: Requires a 'dash pass' and assigned move-in window provided by Housing and Residence Life.

cards.title: Meet Your Orientation Group
cards.subtitle: First Afternoon Gathering
cards.notes: Head to the campus's largest green space to meet your NSO leader and fellow new students for initial introductions.
cards.short_summary: The central hub for orientation group meet-ups and outdoor student social activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation Group Meet-Ups are scheduled on Metzger Lawn from 3–5 p.m. during the first day of Welcome Week.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open public lawn; specific orientation events are for registered new students.

cards.title: Dine at the Caf
cards.subtitle: First Evening Meal
cards.notes: Join the President's Dinner at the main dining hall, featuring multiple food stations including a salad bar and deli.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus dining facility where new students share their first official university meals.
cards.evidence_claim: The President's Dinner is held at the Biola Cafe (the Caf) from 5:30–7 p.m. on the first Friday of orientation.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation Schedule - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Meal plan or payment required; orientation dinners are typically included for new students.

cards.title: Visit the Jesus Mural
cards.subtitle: Iconic Campus Landmark
cards.notes: Stop by Bardwell Hall to see the 27-foot-tall mural of Jesus holding a Bible, a central piece of campus public art.
cards.short_summary: A massive 27-foot mural by Kent Twitchell that serves as a spiritual and artistic landmark on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jesus Mural, titled 'The Word,' is a 27-foot-tall public art piece located on the side of Bardwell Hall.
cards.source_title: Contemplations on the Jesus Mural Decision - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Visible from the exterior of Bardwell Hall at any time.

cards.title: Relax by the Fountain
cards.subtitle: Central Campus Plaza
cards.notes: Gather at this iconic landmark for the Resource Fair or a quiet moment of rest between orientation sessions.
cards.short_summary: A central campus fountain and plaza used for student gatherings and university events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fluor Fountain is an iconic landmark in the center of campus where resource fairs and tours are staged.
cards.source_title: The Fount - Give to Biola University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor public space accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Find a Moment of Quiet
cards.subtitle: 24/7 Prayer Space
cards.notes: Visit the oldest chapel on campus, which is dedicated solely to prayer and reflection with no scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated prayer space open 24/7 for students seeking stillness and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rose of Sharon Prayer Chapel is open any time of the day or night, 365 days a year, for quiet reflection.
cards.source_title: Places for Reflection & Worship - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours daily for individual prayer.

cards.title: Grab a Late Night Coffee
cards.subtitle: Student Union Socializing
cards.notes: Head to the Student Union patio for a caffeine fix and board games with your new roommates.
cards.short_summary: A cozy coffee lounge in the Student Union Building offering drinks and a space for social interaction.
cards.evidence_claim: Common Grounds is a coffee house located on the east patio of the Student Union Building, open for late night study fuel.
cards.source_title: On Campus Dining Locations - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check current semester hours for specific late-night closing times.

cards.title: Attend the Welcome Service
cards.subtitle: Spiritual Commissioning
cards.notes: Participate in this cherished tradition where the university president officially welcomes families and students through prayer and communion.
cards.short_summary: A formal spiritual service marking the official start of the student's journey at Biola.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Welcome and Communion is a special service where President Barry H. Corey officially welcomes new students and families.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Typically held in Chase Gymnasium or Calvary Chapel during orientation weekend.

cards.title: View the Campus from Above
cards.subtitle: Residential Terrace
cards.notes: If you or a friend live in Blackstone, visit the rooftop terrace for a unique view of the La Mirada area.
cards.short_summary: A residential hall feature providing outdoor social space and elevated views of the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Blackstone Hall features a rooftop terrace for student use.
cards.source_title: Blackstone Hall - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Access typically restricted to residents and their guests via keycard.

cards.title: Join the Singspo Tradition
cards.subtitle: Community Worship
cards.notes: End your first weekend by joining fellow students for a night of corporate worship and community commissioning.
cards.short_summary: A high-energy worship event for new students to build community through music.
cards.evidence_claim: New students are officially welcomed and commissioned into the community during the 'Singspo' event.
cards.source_title: New Student Orientation - Biola University
cards.access_notes: Held during orientation weekend for all incoming students.
